title: PASC: Pipeline-Aware Conformal Prediction with Joint Coverage Guarantees for Multi-Stage NLP and LLM Pipelines
authors: Kotte, V. (independent researcher)
problem_setting: Joint coverage certification for a K-stage sequential prediction pipeline (x -> f1 -> z1 -> f2 -> ... -> fK -> zK)
calibration_method: Joint-maximum-nonconformity-score split conformal prediction: per-stage scalar nonconformity scores s_k in [0,1]; take s_max=max_k(s_k) per calibration sample; apply standard split-CP quantile to s_max; Proposition 4 proves intersection of per-stage coverage events equals {max_k s_k <= q}; Theorem 6 gives joint coverage in [1-alpha, 1-alpha+1/(n+1)]
distribution_shift: Tested empirically (CoNLL-2003 in-distribution vs WNUT-17 Twitter vs WikiNEuRal Wikipedia); paper explicitly states the exchangeability-based formal guarantee does not provably extend under shift, though coverage holds empirically in their experiments
workflow_composition: Yes - explicit K-stage pipeline; synthetic scaling study K=1..6; but stages assumed homogeneous (every stage scalarized to a single nonconformity score in [0,1] via a custom per-stage formula) - no agentic/LLM-agent chains tested (named explicitly as future work, not evaluated)
escalation_or_abstention: Not addressed at all - purely a binary accept/reject joint-coverage certification, no selective abstention, no human-review trigger, no automation-coverage tradeoff
evaluation_metrics: Joint coverage vs alpha; compared against independent CP, Bonferroni, tuned Bonferroni, MC Dropout baselines; NER->NED->Entity-Typing pipeline (BERT-base/CoNLL-2003 -> GENRE -> RoBERTa-large/OntoNotes)
main_contribution: Verified: collapses multi-stage joint-coverage problem to single-stage split-CP via a max-nonconformity reduction, giving exact finite-sample joint coverage without a union-bound/Bonferroni penalty
limitations: Own stated limitations (full text): (1) Bonferroni can dominate PASC at high alpha (>=0.20), advantage concentrated in alpha in [0.05,0.10]; (2) formal guarantee requires exchangeability, only empirical (not proven) robustness under covariate shift; (3) marginal coverage only, no conditional/subgroup coverage guarantee (left as future work); (4) assumes every stage can be scalarized to one nonconformity score - does not handle stages with structurally different uncertainty representations (e.g. a bare scalar vs a full distribution + separate confidence field); no escalation/human-review treatment
relevance_to_jev: CLOSEST single paper to the joint-composition half of the research question, now full-text-verified. Directly reusable machinery (max-nonconformity reduction) as a candidate baseline/comparison method for Phase 9. Does NOT cover heterogeneous representation types or escalation policy - both remain open per full-text read.
novelty_implication: Materially narrows the pure 'joint coverage composition' claim for homogeneous-scalar pipelines - that specific sub-problem is solved. Heterogeneous-representation composition and escalation-policy-derived-from-composition remain unaddressed by this paper.

title: Uncertainty Quantification for LLM Agents: A Taxonomy, an Evaluation Protocol, and an Empirical Study
authors: Lin, M.; Lan, Q.; Guan, S.; Jing, W.; Fan, J.; Gregg, D.; Botterweck, G. (corresponding) - Trinity College Dublin; UT Health Science Center Houston; University College Dublin; Northeast Forestry University China
problem_setting: Whether/how step-level calibration relates to trajectory-level calibration in LLM agents
calibration_method: Trajectory-Checkpoint ECE (TC-ECE): a reliability estimator is calibrated if, for EVERY checkpoint index t separately, Pr(Y=1 | R-hat(h_t)=r) = r (probability over trajectories reaching checkpoint t) - explicitly must be assessed per-t, not pooled across (r,t) pairs, because late-checkpoint miscalibration can be masked by early-checkpoint miscalibration of the opposite sign if pooled
workflow_composition: Yes - central topic, and now confirmed FORMALLY PROVEN not just empirical: Proposition 1 gives a two-step correlated-coin-flip counterexample where step-level confidences are perfectly calibrated individually but the naive product of step marginals is miscalibrated at the trajectory level. Proposition 2 quantifies it: P(Y1=1,Y2=1) = p1*p2 + rho*sqrt(p1(1-p1)p2(1-p2)) - under positive inter-step correlation, naive multiplicative composition UNDERESTIMATES true joint success probability
escalation_or_abstention: Diagnostic only - Section 8.2 surveys abstention/clarification/deferral/control as related literature and motivates uncertainty as a signal for when an agent should defer/re-plan/ask/stop, but does not implement or benchmark any escalation/deferral policy itself
evaluation_metrics: Multi-checkpoint calibration measurement across 4 models, 3 experiments, horizons up to 50 steps, on ALFWorld (long-horizon) and a 'Chained-QA' experiment; finds stated agent confidence doesn't consistently beat a step-index baseline, and pooling checkpoints hides late-trajectory overconfidence
main_contribution: Formally proves (not just empirically shows) that per-step calibration does not imply trajectory-level/composed calibration, with an exact quantitative correlation-dependent formula (Prop 2) for how much naive multiplicative composition can be wrong; introduces TC-ECE as a non-pooled per-checkpoint calibration metric; taxonomy spans heterogeneous pipeline LOCATIONS (planning/tool-use, retrieval/memory, multimodal/computer-use, multi-agent coordination)
limitations: Does not attempt a JOINT formal composition/coverage guarantee across stages (unlike PASC, which does) - it is diagnostic, not prescriptive; does not implement/evaluate any escalation policy; heterogeneity covered is about WHERE in a pipeline uncertainty arises (taxonomic axis), not about formally composing stages whose uncertainty REPRESENTATIONS structurally differ in type (distribution vs bare scalar) within one guarantee; Section 11 'open challenges' list could not be fully extracted by the reviewing agent (partial only)
relevance_to_jev: Prop 1/2's correlated-coin-flip result is the direct theoretical validation for this project's own 'conf_product' compositional-reliability statistic (see research/methodology/compositional_reliability_baseline.md) - independent confirmation that naive multiplicative composition of per-node confidence is the wrong null model whenever node correctness is correlated, which is exactly the phenomenon our workflow benchmark is designed to detect empirically via the Delta statistic.
novelty_implication: Materially narrows the 'does per-step calibration compose' half of the question (now proven, not just conjectured, for a 2-step correlated case) - but leaves BOTH joint-composition-with-a-formal-guarantee (PASC's territory) and escalation-policy-derived-from-composition (nobody's territory yet) open.
review_status: VERIFIED FULL TEXT (WebFetch of arxiv.org/html/2609.07395v1, not just abstract); Section 11 only partially extracted - flagged, re-check before final citation
